outcome.technical:
SHAPE: the pre-gate is `meta.buildCommands.preGate`, one command string (several joined with &&), read by `_manifest_vocab.pre_gate_command(build)` -> (command, problem): (None,None) when absent/near-miss spelling/non-object buildCommands, (command,None) when runnable, (None,problem) when blank/non-string/`review-only:`. WHY: buildCommands is the one map a plan already spells commands in; the schema already holds its values to strings (mv72 drives the real validator: number there -> finding), `/audit:task build-command` already sets/drops it (is_derived_step('preGate') is False, so not refused), and nodePreamble already goes in front. A fixed key name with a string value is what the next task (the gate runs it first and stops on its red) can read with one call and no guessing; it needs no schema/COMPATIBILITY/README/panel edit, which a config key (executor.preGate) or a new meta key would (config_vocab_drift checks KNOWN_EXECUTOR against audit-config.schema.json; a meta key needs a schema property or an OFF_SCHEMA row with a false reason). `executor.preGate` is still an unknown config key (pgc1 red if added to KNOWN_EXECUTOR, verified). CONSEQUENCES NOT DONE: being an ordinary buildCommands key, preGate still joins a new phase's default gate like any entry (_manifest_phases is not in my files; P172.3 can skip the duplicate); a plan already using the name preGate for a command of its own will now see it listed (stated in the fragment). NO STOP owed: COMPATIBILITY.md promises meta.version and config keys, not buildCommands names, and does not name lintProbe either; the README's buildCommands row (plugins/audit/README.md, not in my files) could name preGate but no lint demanded it (full sweep green). READERS: audit-lookup.py `pre_gate_reading` (spells through nodePreamble via _evio.resolved_commands); `compose_writer_prompt` lists it in its own block before 'Before you finish' (absent plan: baseline literal unchanged, wp1/wp2 pin it); `compose_executor_brief` adds a `## Pre-gate` section before `What you run` (under executor.runsGate never it names the command and says the executor runs no gate); an unusable value is said in one sentence naming the key. The brief says only 'must pass before you return', not that a gate runs it first. FILES: _config_rules.py untouched (no config key).
